question.text: Which of the following correctly describes eKYC (Electronic KYC) using Aadhaar for mutual fund investments?

answer.text: eKYC allows unlimited investment without any restrictions
UIDAI e-KYC is an accepted KYC verification process and UIDAI data, after client authorization, is sufficient proof of identity and address
eKYC is mandatory and cannot be substituted with physical KYC
eKYC is only available for NRI investors

explanation.text: The Logic: UIDAI e-KYC is accepted as a valid KYC verification process. Once the client authorizes the intermediary to access their Aadhaar data through UIDAI, the demographic information returned by UIDAI is treated as sufficient proof of identity and address. Online KYC can also use OTP sent to the Aadhaar-linked mobile/email along with UIDAI Aadhaar verification. The Trap: Option A ("unlimited investment without any restrictions") is not a feature of eKYC. Option C overstates the position — eKYC is one accepted mode; physical KYC remains available. Option D restricts eKYC to NRIs, which is incorrect. Note: Client authorization to access UIDAI data is the key step that makes UIDAI demographic details acceptable as proof of identity and address for KYC.
